452.name: SqliteBuilder
452.docs: Puts a database together, one entity at a time.

502.name: words
502.docs: What to say when the database refuses something.

17.name: before_save
17.docs: Runs on a record just before it is written, to fit what the table asks for.

15.name: column
15.docs: This field is in a column of another name.

13.name: new
13.docs: On this table, with each field in a column of its name.

363.name: stored
363.docs: The fields that have a column of their own.

261.name: SqliteModelStore
261.docs: Keeps a layer of the model in the database, under a name, as for one person's settings.

311.name: SqliteAttachmentStore
311.docs: Keeps the content of attached files in the database, in a table apart from the records.

209.name: FILES
209.docs: Where the content of attached files is kept.

207.name: MIGRATIONS
207.docs: Where migrations that ran are written down.

155.name: SqlWords
155.docs: What to say when the database refuses something, where `{0}` is the field's caption.

255.name: kind_of
255.docs: What a column holds, by the type SQLite was told; nothing for what a field cannot show.

153.name: rule
153.docs: Any other rule of the table.

455.name: SqliteObjectSpace
455.docs: A unit of work over a [`SqliteDatabase`]. A commit is one transaction.

505.name: managed
505.docs: An entity on a table that is created if it is missing.

555.name: refused
555.docs: Says what the database refused, in words for people.

151.name: unique
151.docs: A value that has to be unique is not.

453.name: builder
453.docs: Starts one on this connection. See [`SqliteBuilder`].

49.name: into
49.docs: Calls `U::from(self)`. That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of [From]<T> for U chooses to do.

451.name: SqliteDatabase
451.docs:
Records in SQLite, on a connection that can be shared with the rest of an application. Any
number of spaces share it.

18.name: after_load
18.docs: Runs on a record just after it is read.

622.name: ravenrs_app_sqlite

16.name: computed
16.docs:
This field is not stored: the database works it out with this SQL expression over the
table, which is trusted as written and never comes from people.

366.name: select
366.docs: A select with every field under its own name, so filters and order by field work.

214.name: Column
214.docs: A column of a table, as SQLite describes it.

12.name: TableMap
12.docs: How an entity lands on a table.

262.name: new
262.docs: A store under this name, creating where it keeps things if needed.

312.name: new
312.docs: A store on this connection, creating where it keeps things if needed.

208.name: SETTINGS
208.docs: Where settings of the model are kept.

156.name: from_texts
156.docs: The texts of a catalog, in its language. What it does not have comes from English.

256.name: entities_from_schema
256.docs:
Entities from the tables a database already has, for an application over a database that came
first: a field per column, a reference per foreign key, and a required field per column that
asks for it. A table with no single key is left out, since a record could not be found. What
comes out is a start: captions and rules are for the application to give.

154.name: failed
154.docs: Anything else, where `{0}` is what SQLite said.

506.name: migration
506.docs:
Runs this once in the life of the database, for what adding a column cannot do, such as
renaming one or moving data. A migration that fails leaves everything as it was.

152.name: in_use
152.docs: Something else still points to the record.

504.name: mapped
504.docs: An entity on a table that exists, whose schema is not touched.
